basics.name: subject
basics.label: Subject
basics.toolTip: Copy the subject value provided by the Grafana App for your connection.

constraints.validationMessage: Paste the subject value shown in the Grafana App.

options.text: Choose where Grafana's identity gets the Monitoring Reader and Monitoring Data Reader roles (the latter is needed for Azure Monitor managed Prometheus). Pick whole subscriptions, individual resource groups, individual resources, or any mix. You need permission to create role assignments at each scope you choose.

elements.name: subscriptionScopes
elements.label: Entire current subscription
elements.toolTip: Grants Monitoring Reader and Monitoring Data Reader on the whole subscription this template is deployed to. For another subscription, run the deployment in that subscription.

elements.name: resourceGroupScopes
elements.label: Resource groups (in the current subscription)
elements.toolTip: Grants Monitoring Reader and Monitoring Data Reader on every resource in each selected resource group.

elements.name: resourceScopes
elements.label: Individual resources (in the current subscription)
elements.toolTip: Grants Monitoring Reader and Monitoring Data Reader on only the selected resources.

elements.name: info
elements.visible: [not(empty(filter(coalesce(steps('scopes').kustoApi.value, parse('[]')), (c) => or(contains(map(steps('scopes').subscriptionScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(concat('/subscriptions/', subscription().subscriptionId))), contains(map(steps('scopes').resourceGroupScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(substring(c.id, 0, indexOf(c.id, '/providers/')))), contains(map(steps('scopes').resourceScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(c.id))))))]

options.text: We found Azure Data Explorer (Kusto) clusters in the scopes you selected. Monitoring Reader does not give query access to Kusto, which has its own permission model. Select the clusters Grafana should be able to query.

elements.name: clusterWideWarning
elements.visible: [not(empty(filter(coalesce(steps('scopes').kustoApi.value, parse('[]')), (c) => or(contains(map(steps('scopes').subscriptionScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(concat('/subscriptions/', subscription().subscriptionId))), contains(map(steps('scopes').resourceGroupScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(substring(c.id, 0, indexOf(c.id, '/providers/')))), contains(map(steps('scopes').resourceScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(c.id))))))]

options.text: This grants the AllDatabasesViewer role, which is cluster-wide: Grafana's identity will be able to read every database on each selected cluster, including databases created in the future. You need write access on each selected cluster.

elements.name: kustoClusterIds
elements.label: Clusters to grant AllDatabasesViewer on
elements.toolTip: Only clusters inside the scopes you selected in the previous step are listed. Leave empty to skip.
elements.visible: [not(empty(filter(coalesce(steps('scopes').kustoApi.value, parse('[]')), (c) => or(contains(map(steps('scopes').subscriptionScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(concat('/subscriptions/', subscription().subscriptionId))), contains(map(steps('scopes').resourceGroupScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(substring(c.id, 0, indexOf(c.id, '/providers/')))), contains(map(steps('scopes').resourceScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(c.id))))))]

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(coalesce(steps('scopes').kustoApi.value, parse('[]')), (c) => or(contains(map(steps('scopes').subscriptionScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(concat('/subscriptions/', subscription().subscriptionId))), contains(map(steps('scopes').resourceGroupScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(substring(c.id, 0, indexOf(c.id, '/providers/')))), contains(map(steps('scopes').resourceScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(c.id)))), (item) => parse(concat('{"label":"', item.name, '","value":"', item.id, '"}')))]

elements.name: noClusters
elements.visible: [and(not(equals(coalesce(steps('scopes').kustoApi.value, 'loading'), 'loading')), empty(filter(coalesce(steps('scopes').kustoApi.value, parse('[]')), (c) => or(contains(map(steps('scopes').subscriptionScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(concat('/subscriptions/', subscription().subscriptionId))), contains(map(steps('scopes').resourceGroupScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(substring(c.id, 0, indexOf(c.id, '/providers/')))), contains(map(steps('scopes').resourceScopes, (s) => toLower(s)), toLower(c.id))))))]

options.text: No Azure Data Explorer clusters were found in the scopes you selected, so there is nothing to configure here. Click Next.

elements.name: resourceGroupMode
elements.label: Resource group
elements.toolTip: Where the managed identity lives. Choose an existing group or create a new one.

elements.name: newResourceGroupName
elements.label: New resource group name
elements.toolTip: A new resource group is created in the deployment region. If a group with this name already exists, choose Use existing instead.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid resource group name.

elements.name: existingResourceGroupName
elements.label: Existing resource group
elements.toolTip: Resource group to place the managed identity in.

elements.name: managedIdentityName
elements.label: Managed identity name override (optional)

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid managed identity name.

elements.toolTip: Advanced. Leave empty: a unique name (mi-grafana-<hash>) is generated for this connection and shown in the deployment outputs. Set a name only to pin or reuse a specific identity; connections that share an identity overwrite each other's subject.
